issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires Farm to use a List (implemented with an ArrayList) for its animals and to initialize that ArrayList in the no-argument constructor. The solution implementation uses a Set<Animal> (HashSet) for the animals field and provides getter/setter returning Set<Animal>. This is a structural mismatch: the field type, constructor initialization and accessor signatures differ from the specification. Students following the instructions (using List/ArrayList and List-typed getter/setter) would produce code that does not match the solution; conversely, students inspecting the solution would be confused because it contradicts the written requirement. Using a Set also changes collection semantics (no guaranteed order, unique elements), which can affect expected behavior of methods like singFarmSong() and feedAllAnimals().
issues.suggested_fix: Align the solution with the problem statement: change the Farm.animals field type to List<Animal>, initialize it with new ArrayList<>() in the no-argument constructor, and update the getter and setter to use List<Animal>. This preserves the educational intent (teaching List/ArrayList usage) and ensures template, specification, and solution are consistent. Concretely: (1) replace 'private Set<Animal> animals;' with 'private List<Animal> animals;'; (2) import java.util.ArrayList and java.util.List and initialize 'this.animals = new ArrayList<>();' in the constructor; (3) change getAnimals()/setAnimals() signatures to return/accept List<Animal>.
